`EmitterOutcome` (`src/sim/emitter/emitter_outcome.gd`, `RefCounted`, caller-owned and reused): `code: int`, `id: int`, `count: int`. A Class B mutator keeps `-> void` and clamps, never rejects, never calls `scope.fault`; an unknown id is a no-op that sets `out.code`. Callers hold one outcome object per call site, so a call allocates nothing.

**D3.5 Binding source (TR-emitter-009).** `binding_source(ctx)` is the descriptor field and `ctx.put`s a flat `PackedInt64Array` `[player_id, beam_id, ...]` in **ascending `player_id`**, even length, built from the beam rows (`kind == BEAM`, `owner_ref` the PlayerId) into a pre-sized scratch array and duplicated for the `put` (ADR-0016 sections 6.1 and 6.2; the GDD's `[(player_id, beam_id)]` list becomes this flat array, a GDD sync item). `toggle_beam` carries `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` with source `emitter.state`, and the first tick of a restored run passes the authority check because the kernel's LOADING rebuild binds from this source after every `post_restore` (ADR-0016 KRN-RST-06).

**D3.6 Closed transition table and the invalid-transition counter (TR-emitter-045).** The record lifecycle (ABSENT, OFF, ARMING, ON, STARVED, WANING) and the subject bit (UNREGISTERED, UNLIT, LIT) are two small tables in `src/shared/emitter/emitter_kind.gd` as data (`TRANSITIONS_RECORD`, `TRANSITIONS_BIT`: a `from * N + to` bitmask over a closed list). Every state change in `src/sim/emitter/` goes through `EmitterDerived.move_state(row, to)`, which checks the table: an unlisted pair leaves the state unchanged, increments `emitter_invalid_transition[from * STATES + to]` (a `PackedInt32Array` of `STATES * STATES` counters in `EmitterDiag`, labelled by from and to in the dump) and reports through `Diagnostics` in a debug build (no `assert(`). The record state itself is **derived** (computed from `switch_on`, `arm_tick`, `served_pm`, liveness and life); `move_state` is the choke point that audits each derived change against the closed table and is what AC-109 drives with an injected illegal request (for example WANING to OFF).

**D3.7 Commit-spacing guard lives in the commit path too (TR-emitter-011, TR-light-033).** `toggle_beam.validate` rejects `TOO_SOON` and `set_switch.validate` rejects `COOLDOWN` when `last_toggle_tick >= 0` and `commit_tick - last_toggle_tick < SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`, with `commit_tick` per D.2b: the apply tick for a beam toggle, for an OFF that darkens a lit or armed lamp and for every switch of a self-powered fixture; `arm_tick` (D5.2) for the ON of a Graph-powered lamp; an OFF applied while ARMING is exempt and writes nothing; E10 and `force_off` are exempt. **The guard is also enforced where the transition is committed** (TR-light-033: "a command-level spacing guard alone is proven insufficient under arming-latency jitter"): W1 writes `last_toggle_tick = arm_tick` at the run in which an ON is realised and compares it with the previous value; a realised transition closer than `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (reachable only through arming-latency jitter that `validate` could not foresee, or a non-`validate` writer) increments the release counter `emitter_flash_rate_defect`, is **still committed** (refusing here would make the light disagree with the committed switch, and Lighting's flash governor may not retime a committed switch) and reports through `Diagnostics` in a debug build. The "at most three flashes per second" arithmetic is the I-SPACING derivation (D15.1).

**D3.8 `toggle_beam` and Suit.** `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view for `CHARGE_EMPTY` (`SuitView.beam_charge_pm(player_id)`, an ADR-0027 assumption in `cross_adr_assumptions`); a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge. Suit's `suit.vitals` hook (before `emitter.place` in the compiled order) reads the beam record `lit` and calls E5 at charge zero, so a `force_off` takes effect in the same tick's run. A BEAM record's `lit` and `output_of` derive from its own canonical `switch_on` and `BEAM_BASE_PM` and from no late-mutable upstream block, so this read is **exempt** from the derived-read restriction of D14.4 (the restriction covers lamp-kind records, subjects and `section_emission`). The beam is a suit load and never calls M14.

18:**D4.2 No snapshot copy (decided; revises the mechanism of TR-emitter-025, not its intent).** EM-25 specifies a per-tick snapshot "built once in W7" so that readers see stable columns. This ADR does not build one. The subject table and the emitter derived columns are written **only inside `emitter.place`** (outside the hook, the only derived writers are E10 and the creation mutators, each for the record's own derived fields, D2.5, D3.4); the kernel is single-threaded and the presentation stages run between ticks (ADR-0009), so any read outside `emitter.place` already sees a committed table, and no reader runs *inside* the hook. A copy would cost `W_SNAP` units per emitter every tick (D.14 prices it at about 4 % of `B` at the typical point) to protect against a race that cannot occur. What TR-emitter-025 asks for survives: reads are pure table lookups (typed scalar getters over packed columns, ascending id by construction), at most one tick stale unless the reader declares `after: [emitter.place]`, allocation-free, never callable from a notification handler that decides state, with the no-retain rule kept for list reads (they fill a caller-owned buffer, D13.1). `T_snap` leaves the budget model; the per-section emission array of D.12 is accumulated in W2 and made current in W7, and a late-created (`pending`) emitter is absent from it until the next run, the same one-tick lag as the subject table.

This ADR does not build one. **D1.1 Purity split.** The exposure kernel is pure functions of ints so that unit tests, the content lint (TR-derelict-038: "console, arrival and wake-room lighting proved headlessly") and the block call the same code. `ExposureProbe` composes the kernel with a caller-supplied `OccluderSource` double and plain emitter fields; it is **not** the VS-A `probe(body_id, point)` read (deferred and lint-banned in MVP source) and is importable from `src/sim/` only inside `testing/` and the boot checks.

**D1.2 What is data (decided).** The shape table (11 rows, EM-8), the hue token set and every tunable are **stage-1 content**, not code constants: `assets/data/emitter/{shape_table,hue_map,emitter_tuning}.json` plus the Failure & Trail glow rows in `assets/data/failure_trail/glow_table.json` (ADR-0007 section 1.1; architecture IC-12). Reasons: gameplay values are data-driven (coding standards); the technical artist owns the placeholders and re-tunes after the Lighting spike; and the Item DB `emits` clause (TR-emitter-043, TR-itemdb-034) needs a table to validate against at load, which ADR-0007 section 1.4 says the loader must **read from the Emitter's published table and not copy** (stage 1 loads before the Item DB, section 1.7). **`ShapeCatalog` is that published table.** Its authored columns are `shape_id`, `curve_class`, `geometry` (`ONE_CONE`, `TWO_CONES`, `OMNI`), `half_angle_units`, `split_axis_units`, `reach_px`, `gates_actions`, `shadow_casting` (informational) and `art_ref`; the freeze **derives** `cos2_q28` from `DirTable` (the square of the Q14 cosine at `half_angle_units`) instead of storing a second hand-typed integer, so the table, the direction table and the I-OVERFLOW bound cannot disagree. The five derived values equal the GDD's EM-8 column exactly (probed, section 17). The art-bible degrees stay in the art bible; `tools/emitter/check_shapes.gd` checks each `half_angle_units` against its degree figure (float allowed there) and fails the build on drift over its tolerance.

**D1.3 The direction table is generated code, not content (decided).** `DirTable.UX`/`UY` are mathematical constants (two `AIM_UNITS`-entry `Array[int]` consts), not designer data, so they bypass the content loader: a lint or test can use them with no `ContentSet`, and an engine change cannot reorder a JSON array under them. ADR-0007 Alternative 2 (code-as-data) is rejected for *content*; it does not cover a derived mathematical table, and `tools/emitter/gen_dir_table.gd` plus a CI byte-diff gate (`EMT-GOLD-01`) make regeneration a build step with a golden hash. **Source of truth (E6):** the committed `dir_table.gd` is the source of truth, and the golden hash of its contents is checked on every CI platform; the generator runs on every CI platform but only one designated platform's output is byte-diffed against the committed file, because GDScript `cos`/`sin` call the platform libm (MSVC on Windows, glibc on Linux) and a last-ulp difference at a `round()` tie is possible with no real defect behind it (P2 was probed on Windows only). The named fallback, if a cross-OS mismatch is ever seen, is an integer-only CORDIC or Taylor generation of the first quadrant in the tool, so that the table does not depend on libm at all. Generation: the first quadrant `a = 0..AIM_UNITS/4` is computed in the tool as `round(16384 * cos/sin(a * TAU / AIM_UNITS))`, and the other three are filled **by reflection**, never recomputed (`DIR[AIM_UNITS/2 - a] = (-ux, uy)`, `DIR[AIM_UNITS - a] = (ux, -uy)`), then `uy` is negated so that aim `3 * AIM_UNITS / 4` is `(0, +16384)` (south, screen y down, EM-19). I-MIRROR is therefore true by construction and re-asserted at boot. **Probed:** `const X: PackedInt32Array = PackedInt32Array([...])` fails to parse ("isn't a constant expression"); `const X: Array[int] = [...]` loads (4,096 elements, `is_read_only()` true). The kernel reads `DirTable.UX[a]` directly in `@hot` code (an indexed read of a typed constant array: no copy, no allocation). The table length must equal `AIM_UNITS` (boot invariant `I-DIRSIZE`).

**D1.4 Square-root table (decided).** The distance `d = floor(sqrt(d2))` of D.7 is the largest `k` with `k*k <= d2`, found by the native `bsearch` of a boot-built `PackedInt32Array` of squares (`SQ[k] = k*k`, `k = 0..REACH_MAX_PX + 1`) owned by `EmitterDerived` and passed to the kernel (`static var` is banned, so the table is an instance field, not a global). **Call form (E1):** `floor_root(sq, d2) = sq.bsearch(d2, false) - 1`, a single shared function (`ConeMath.floor_root` in `src/shared/emitter/`; if Foundation prefers it in `IntMath` as `IntMath.isqrt_table`, the signature is unchanged) used by the block, the content lint and the tests, with a fixture over every `d2` in its precondition range. The default `bsearch(v, before = true)` returns the lower-bound insertion index and is **wrong for every non-square `d2`** (probed on squares `[0,1,4,9,16,25,...]`: `bsearch(16)` = 4 is right, `bsearch(17)` = 5 is wrong, the floor root is 4; with `before = false` and `- 1` there were 0 failures over `d2` 0..81, P7). **Precondition:** `0 <= d2 <= (REACH_MAX_PX + 1)^2`, so the result stays in `0..REACH_MAX_PX + 1` and the table has `REACH_MAX_PX + 2` entries. Exactness is a boot invariant (`I-SQRT`: for every `d2` in `0..(REACH_MAX_PX + 1)^2` the result `r` of the shared function satisfies `r*r <= d2 < (r+1)*(r+1)`, so the invariant tests the same code the hot path calls). ### D.2 Switch latency

The `switch_latency` formula is defined as:

`arm_tick = T_a + ((GRAPH_STEP_TICKS − (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)) mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`, `L = arm_tick − T_a`; the negative case (A1 false, a Graph that consumes only strictly later requests) is `arm_tick′ = T_a + GRAPH_STEP_TICKS − (T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `T_a` | int | ≥ 0 | kernel clock | the tick whose P2 applies `set_switch` / `set_beacon`; **or the creation tick of an E1 authored-on lamp or beacon** (0 at `init_world`, which runs in LOADING before the first RUNNING tick; the range is widened from ≥ 1 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) |
| `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int | 6 | registry (locked) | Graph hooks run at divisor 6; under the baseline stagger (LS-8: power 0, atmo 2, failure 4) the power hook, which consumes M14, runs at offset 0, so for input timing a Graph tick is `T mod 6 = 0` (EM-1, terminology) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
| `arm_tick` | int | `T_a`..`T_a + 5` | calculated | the first Graph tick whose phase 0 consumes the queued M14 request; the lamp is ARMING (`output_pm` 0) before it |
| `L` | int | 0..5 | calculated | ticks from apply to lit; switching off is `L = 0` |

**New-game example (E1, authored-on home-ship lamp)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `init_world` runs at clock 0 and Web Map's E1 creates the home-ship's authored-on lamp (`switch_on` true, rated draw 20 W). `T_a` 0 is a Graph tick, so `arm_tick` = 0 and `L` = 0 (negative case 6): M14 `set_load_request(node_ref, 20)` is queued inside E1 and the Graph's phase 0 of tick 0 consumes it (assumption A1; A3 below); the lamp is ARMING until then and lit by tick 0's `emitter.place`, with the Graph carrying the 20 W request from tick 0 — the first frame the player sees shows a lit lamp and a drawn request that agree. `last_toggle_tick` is written 0 at that tick. **Assumption A3** *(new)*: the first RUNNING tick is the clock value `init_world` ran at (tick 0), not 1; if the kernel starts RUNNING at tick 1, `T_a` 0 gives `arm_tick` 0 which no run consumes, and E1 must use `T_a` = 1 (`arm_tick` 6); the kernel's owner confirms (cross-GDD note). **Output Range:** `L` in 0..5 ticks (0..83 ms); the negative case 1..6. The hook is `after: graph.propagate.failure` (EM-1), so the lamp is lit by the `emitter.place` of the same tick as `arm_tick`. **Example:** `T_a` 1200 (a Graph tick) → `arm_tick` 1200, `L` 0 (negative case 1206, `L` 6); `T_a` 1201 → 1206, `L` 5; `T_a` 1205 → 1206, `L` 1. Inrush (the Graph's business, visible as an honest dip): eight lamps switched together on a tier-3 island with 700 W free request 8 × ⌊20 × `INRUSH_PM` / 1000⌋ = 240 W plus a neighbouring 500 W heater, so `served_pm` = ⌊1000 × 700 / 740⌋ = 945 for `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 runs (0.5 s), then 1000.

212:**D5.1 Lamp output (TR-emitter-014).** `LampMath.lamp_output(base_pm, served_pm, switch_on, armed, live) -> int` is `IntMath.floor_div(base_pm * served_pm, 1000)` when `switch_on`, `armed` and `live` hold, else 0. `served_pm` is the tier's satisfaction read live each run from `GraphView.served_pm(node_id)` (ADR-0011 section 9.1; persisted as `n_served` per ADR-0012, so it is exact straight after a restore); the Emitter's own `switch_on` gates the light (a switched-off lamp can still read `served_pm` 1000). A lamp is **live** iff `GraphView.node_live(node_ref)` (ADR-0011 section 9: O(1), allocation-free, false for an unknown or tombstoned id; every other getter returns its documented neutral value for a non-live id and `node_state` returns `GraphIds.STATE_NONE`, -1, which is outside the enum, so liveness is decided by the guard and never from a neutral value; CT-09), the node is not dormant (`section_dormant`), and `node_state` is not FAILED, DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT (EM-13). A not-live lamp keeps `switch_on` and relights on repair with no command. A node with `node_ref` 0 (the two self-powered subkinds) has no liveness test, no ARMING and a fixed `base_pm`.
214:**D5.2 Arming latency (TR-emitter-013).** `arm_tick` is the first tick at or after the apply tick `T_a` on which a power hook runs: `arm_tick = T_a + IntMath.posmod_i(power_offset - T_a, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`, with `power_offset` and `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` read from the frozen `GraphTuning` catalog injected at `setup()` (ADR-0012 makes the hook offsets tuning data, so the GDD's `T_a mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` form, which assumes offset 0, is generalised; at offset 0 the two are identical, which is a unit test). This agrees with ADR-0012's drain rule (a P2 apply on a power-hook tick is drained by the same tick's phase 0; an apply on any other tick by the next power-hook tick), so a lamp is ARMING with output 0 for 0 to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks and is lit by the first `emitter.place` at or after `arm_tick`. OFF is immediate with M14 `(node_ref, 0)`. M14 is called **inside the apply** through the injected Graph mutator object (`views` cannot write; the Graph's published mutators are wired by the composition root, ADR-0003 section 7). **Hard dependency (T5, CT-36):** E1 calls M14 under the INIT scope at Web Map's `init_world`, so ADR-0012 must list M14 as `APPLY, HOOK, INIT` and carry the INIT drain row: an INIT deposit drains at phase 0 of the first `graph.propagate.power` run after LOADING to RUNNING, which is the first RUNNING tick `T` with `T mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == hook_offset_power`. **That tick is `arm_tick` for an INIT-scope creation:** `T_a` is the first RUNNING tick (one more than the N2 clock `T` the INIT pass is stamped with, ADR-0016 section 1.1, CT-43), so the formula above gives exactly ADR-0012's drain tick. The fallback of creating authored-on Graph lamps with `switch_on` set and no M14 call is not taken (ADR-0012 grants M14 in INIT scope). The negative case of D.2 (a Graph that consumes only strictly later requests) is a `GraphTuning` fact the unit tests parameterise, not a second code path.
216:**D5.3 Beam pose and the occlusion origin (TR-emitter-016).** For the seat's BEAM: `origin` (the apex of the cone and the distance origin) is the chest point read at the time of the run as two scalars, `ControllerView.get_chest_x(player_id)` and `get_chest_y(player_id)` (ADR-0019, CT-28: absolute body-frame ints computed on every read from the same tick's `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` plus the frozen `CHEST_POINT[sheet][row]` for the current `loco_state`, mirrored by facing; O(1), allocation-free, so it cannot lag the position; the Emitter takes the two values once per beam per run); the axis is the committed `ControllerView.get_aim_angle(player_id)` (`AIM_UNITS`; the beam follows aim, not facing); `ControllerView.get_loco_state(player_id)` gives the DEAD/DOWNED/STAGGERED/IN_POD behaviour below; reach, `half_angle_units` and curve class come from the shape row of `shape_id` (`ShapeCatalog`); `BEAM_BASE_PM` is the output while on (no low-charge dimming in the MVP); the `HAND_POINT` is never read. **The occlusion segment starts at the foot** (`pos_curr`, `BodyView.pos_x/_y(actor)`), because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction (`LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them) and is free of the chest jitter (EM-6, the technical-director's ruling). The whole rule lives in one function, `EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin(row, out_xy)`; ADR-0018 (the Lighting spike) consumes `EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin(row, out_xy)` (CT-30), and **outcome D replaces `occlusion_origin` and adds a hot, allocation-free `EmitterView` read of the beam's previous and current occlusion origin (two int pairs, derived each tick) and the `OCC_ORIGIN_MODE` tuning row, introduced together with ADR-0018's combination invariant; there is no change while B or A ships** (the reads and the tuning row are not reserved now: the only reachable mode pairs at ship are legal, so the invariant could never fire). Other kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both apex and occlusion. The BEAM_SPILL (shape row 11, present only while the beam is on and `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` is above zero) is a **second dynamic item of the beam record**, SOFT, omnidirectional, centred on the foot origin, output `BEAM_SPILL_PM`, gating actions, not stored as an emitter, absent from `emitters()` and from `section_emission`; it runs through the same radius-then-occlusion pipeline and its changes dirty the beam's own key. DOWNED keeps the beam committed (aim frozen); DEAD forces it off in W1; STAGGERED leaves it unchanged; IN_POD follows the actor into the pod body's frame.
218:**D5.4 Node lantern (TR-emitter-015).** `output_pm = IntMath.floor_div(base_pm * clampi(run_pm, 0, 1000), 1000)` when the node is live and its `node_state` is in the Item DB's `lantern_on_states` bitmask, with `run_pm` the Graph-published `GraphView.run_pm(id)` consumed as published and clamped (never recomputed from `out_w`, never `served_pm` alone, no fallback form: a lantern that cannot read `run_pm` is a boot defect). The lantern roster is Item DB data (`emits.shape == LANTERN`), not a list here.
220:**D5.5 Beacon (TR-emitter-029).** `BeaconMath.aim(phase, dir, T, sweep_ticks) = IntMath.posmod_i(phase + dir * IntMath.floor_div(T * AIM_UNITS, sweep_ticks), AIM_UNITS)` with `T` the kernel tick and `dir` +1 or -1: no per-tick angle state, so save-equivalence is automatic (the kernel clock is persisted). `T * AIM_UNITS` stays below 2^62 (I-OVERFLOW bounds `T` below 2^50). The beacon's brightness is the lamp formula (it carries a `node_ref` in the MVP), `gates_actions` is **false** (`ShapeCatalog` row 8), it is a dynamic-layer item, and a `set_beacon` ON starts from the angle the pure function gives at that tick. `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` is `EmitterTuning`; any positive integer is valid.

**EM-22 — `lit(subject)`: threshold, hysteresis and the beacon exception.** `lit(ref)` is a hysteresis filter over `act_lux_pm` (Formulas D.8): it becomes true when `act_lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM`, becomes false when `act_lux_pm < LIT_OFF_PM`, and holds between. Placeholders `LIT_ON_PM` 150 (range 100–300) and `LIT_OFF_PM` 120 (60–140), the `LIT_THRESHOLD_PM` family **owned by the technical-artist** (art bible 7.0: "the illumination threshold that enables prompt and inspect-card drawing"), confirmed against the rendered edge in the Lighting spike (8.12 step 2). A newly registered subject starts unlit and is evaluated at the next `emitter.place`. A hard-edged rim is a *step* (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel), which the 150/120 hysteresis never sees; rim chatter while a beam sweeps is held by the Controller's committed-aim quantisation (`AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` 32 units) and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6), and the hysteresis bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning glowsticks, fixture pools). There is **no dwell** (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` fixed at 0): keeping `lit` true after the light went would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie. `lit(ref)` and `lux(ref)` are separate answers because the beacon's sweep must not strobe prompts (EM-16). **The hysteresis bit is canonical** (checkpoint ruling CP-2): `lit(ref)` depends on last tick's answer, and a subject whose `act_lux_pm` sits between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` has no other source for its bit, so by EM-4's own definition the bit is a discrete fact — one bit per registered subject, at most `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` bits, snapshotted and hashed. `post_restore` rebuilds `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `top_emitter_id` from the restored emitters and **keeps the bit**; the next `emitter.place` applies hysteresis normally. ### 14. Restore, save-equivalence and the verifier (TR-emitter-007, -008, -028 (restore part), -038 (payload side))

**D14.1 `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)`.** Two-phase per block (ADR-0016 section 3): `restore` validates and copies the persisted columns **into the existing block object** (never replaces it, so `EmitterView` stays valid) and touches nothing else. **Every incoming column is duplicated (E3, CT-41):** `restore()` owns nothing in the payload (ADR-0016 section 3.1), so it assigns `state.col = staged["col"].duplicate()` (or resizes and copies into the existing array) for every `Packed*Array` and `duplicate(true)` for any nested container, and never keeps a reference to a payload array (packed arrays are shared by reference in GDScript and `Dictionary.duplicate()` is shallow, ADR-0006 probe 16; an aliasing restore would let the live block mutate the kernel's staged payload and a retry or second restore of the same payload would see live state). The 4.7 rule that a packed-element write skips the setter does not affect this block: no setter is used and dirty keys are marked explicitly; every derived structure is the job of `post_restore`. Validation order, first failure wins, each through `ctx.fault(code)` with no partial application: unsupported `stored_version` or a key set that differs from the allow-list (`EMITTER_RESTORE_SCHEMA`; a reported failure, never a silent default); ragged column lengths, non-ascending or duplicate ids or refs (`EMITTER_RESTORE_COLUMNS`); `next_emitter_id` not above every id, `last_place_tick` or `fault_step_seen` out of range (`EMITTER_RESTORE_COUNTER`); an enum, flag or numeric column out of its range, including every byte column against 0..255 (`priority`, `subkind`, `shape_id`) and every Int32 column against its declared bound, since a wrapped value is a corrupt save (E2), a count above a cap (`EMITTER_RESTORE_RANGE`); a `section_id`, `shape_id`, `hue_id`, `glow_key` or `node_ref` that does not resolve against the catalogs and the already-restored Layout and Graph (`EMITTER_RESTORE_REF`); a subject-table violation: an ACTOR row with non-zero derived columns, `pending` outside 0..2, a pending anchor without its flag, the moving cap exceeded (`EMITTER_RESTORE_SUBJECTS`). The verifier of D14.3 is the same function the runtime tests reuse.

**D14.2 `post_restore(ctx)`: the cold build of the table the last run committed, over end-of-tick upstream state.** It runs after every predecessor in the `restore_after` DAG has restored **and** post-restored (ADR-0016 section 4.1), so Layout's door leaves, the Graph's intensive caches (`P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, the pressure trend) and topology caches, and Body are valid (Tier D reads of DAG predecessors only); `served_pm`, the band memory and the Controller's chest point are not Tier D (persisted `n_served` and band columns, and a read-time getter with nothing derived, ADR-0016 section 3.4). It writes derived members only: no clamp, no prune, no repair, no cross-block write, and no canonical column either (the `lit` bits stay as `restore` set them). In ascending id: the section cache and frames (after the cold build the cache is seeded with the current version triple, offset and `body_id` read after Layout's `post_restore`, D11.4); the record derived fields with `T_derive = hdr.last_place_tick`; the slot stores, grids and `by_id`/`by_ref` ranks; the static layer for the **applied** view (D2.5) as the cold class (scenario S6); rows pending at the snapshot stay pending until W3 of the first run at T+1, as in the live run, so the pending set equals the live run's at T+1; the movers' static sweep; the dynamic layer as it stood at that run; the W6 sums (`lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm`, `top_emitter_id`) with each `lit` bit copied verbatim and `LitHysteresis.next` never called (D9.5 (b)); the emission array; the last-emitted dirty buckets and reaches; `static_epoch` and the tally reset. FAULT_GLOW rows are not touched (D6.4). **Idempotence:** calling `post_restore` twice in a row on the same restored block leaves every derived column and the block hash unchanged (tested); two restores of the same bytes under different valid linear extensions of the `restore_after` DAG produce identical per-tick `state_hash` traces and read-view answers (the ADR-0016 KRN-RST-05 battery, extended with `lit`, `lux`, `top_emitter`, `r_lit_of`, `section_emission` and the fixtures of D2.5).
